items.title: Evacuations begin in occupied Ukrainian town as Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire holds
items.brief: Hundreds of people from an occupied town in southern Ukraine who survived months without basic supplies are being evacuated on Friday under a ceasefire agreement negotiated by first lady Melania Trump .

items.title: ‘They killed us’: Russia’s last independent newspaper falls silent amid pressure from Kremlin
items.brief: Novaya Gazeta , one of Russia’s last independent news outlets, announced on Friday it would close down operations due to pressure from authorities.

items.title: World’s largest crypto exchange hit by suspected North Korean hack in world’s largest heist
items.brief: Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has suspended withdrawals after hackers broke into its digital wallets and stole $6 billion in what appears to be the biggest crypto heist ever.

items.title: Major anti-government protests sweep across Italy
items.brief: Farmers dumped manure on the streets of Turin on Friday as mass demonstrations unfurled across more than 50 cities in Italy.

items.title: Christa Pike, in first public comments since botched execution: ‘Healing is not the same as being okay’
items.brief: Christa Pike , who survived Tennessee’s attempt to execute her by lethal injection a month ago, is speaking out for the first time, saying she is recovering, “but healing is not the same as being okay.”

items.title: Visit Norway makes toilets ‘great again’ after Trump’s ‘sh*t house country’ jab
items.brief: Norway’s tourism board has launched a tongue-in-cheek toilet campaign to show off the country’s most scenic restrooms after US President Donald Trump branded the Nordic nation a “sh*t house country.”

items.title: Pope Leo makes history by voting in US midterms
items.brief: Pope Leo XIV has submitted a mail-in ballot for the US midterms, becoming the first pope to vote in a US election and likely the first to vote in a secular democratic election.
